"""The command line: one sub-command per job done at the counter."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from datetime import date

from . import api
from .config import DATA_DIR, LIBRARY_NAME
from .errors import BookshelfError


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """The parser behind ``python -m bookshelf``."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="bookshelf",
        description=f"{LIBRARY_NAME} counter tools.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", default=DATA_DIR, help="where the JSON tables are kept")
    parser.add_argument("--today", default=None, help="the date to judge lateness against")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    commands.add_parser("list", help="list every title the library owns")

    add = commands.add_parser("add", help="add a title to the catalogue")
    add.add_argument("isbn")
    add.add_argument("title")
    add.add_argument("author")
    add.add_argument("--copies", type=int, default=1)

    borrow = commands.add_parser("borrow", help="lend a copy to a member")
    borrow.add_argument("isbn")
    borrow.add_argument("card_number")

    commands.add_parser("overdue", help="list the loans that are late")
    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Run one counter command and print what it returned, as JSON."""
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    catalog, register = api.build_services(args.data_dir)
    today = date.fromisoformat(args.today) if args.today else date.today()
    try:
        if args.command == "list":
            result: object = api.list_titles(catalog)
        elif args.command == "add":
            result = api.add_title(catalog, args.isbn, args.title, args.author, args.copies)
        elif args.command == "borrow":
            result = api.borrow_title(register, args.isbn, args.card_number, today)
        else:
            result = api.overdue_report(register, today)
    except BookshelfError as error:
        print(json.dumps(api.describe_failure(error), indent=2, sort_keys=True))
        return 1
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    return 0

"""Settings for the lending service: no other module reads the environment."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os

DEFAULT_LOAN_DAYS = 21
MAX_LOANS_PER_MEMBER = 5
RENEWAL_LIMIT = 2
LIBRARY_NAME = "Fennel Street Library"

# The data directory is the one setting that really does change between one
# deployment and the next, so it is the one setting read from the environment.
DATA_DIR = os.environ.get("BOOKSHELF_DATA_DIR", "var/bookshelf")


def loan_length_days(renewals: int) -> int:
    """How long a loan runs, given how often it has already been renewed.

    Renewed loans are shorter, so a title in demand comes back sooner.
    """
    if renewals <= 0:
        return DEFAULT_LOAN_DAYS
    return max(7, DEFAULT_LOAN_DAYS - 7 * renewals)

"""How the library tells members about the books they are holding."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Protocol

from .config import LIBRARY_NAME

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from datetime import date

    from .models import Loan, Member

REMINDER_WINDOW_DAYS = 3


class Notifier(Protocol):
    """Anything that can put one message in front of one member."""

    def send(self, member: Member, subject: str, body: str) -> None:
        """Deliver the message, however this channel delivers messages."""


@dataclass
class _RecordedMessage:
    """One message a :class:`RecordingNotifier` was asked to send."""

    card_number: str
    subject: str
    body: str


class RecordingNotifier:
    """A notifier that keeps messages in memory instead of sending them.

    What the service runs on until a real channel is configured.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._sent: list[_RecordedMessage] = []

    @property
    def sent(self) -> list[_RecordedMessage]:
        """Every message this notifier has been handed, oldest first."""
        return list(self._sent)

    def send(self, member: Member, subject: str, body: str) -> None:
        """Record the message instead of delivering it anywhere."""
        self._sent.append(_RecordedMessage(member.card_number, subject, body))

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Forget everything recorded so far."""
        self._sent.clear()


def due_soon_message(loan: Loan, days_left: int) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """The subject and body of the reminder sent before a loan falls due."""
    subject = f"{LIBRARY_NAME}: a book is due back in {days_left} days"
    body = (
        f"ISBN {loan.isbn} is due back on {loan.window.due.isoformat()}. "
        "You can renew it at the counter or on the library's website."
    )
    return subject, body


async def remind_member(
    notifier: Notifier, member: Member, loans: list[Loan], today: date
) -> int:
    """Send one reminder per loan that is nearly due, and count what was sent.

    This is a coroutine because a real channel would wait on the network.
    The in-memory notifier finishes without waiting for anything.
    """
    sent = 0
    for loan in loans:
        days_left = loan.days_left(today)
        if 0 <= days_left <= REMINDER_WINDOW_DAYS:
            subject, body = due_soon_message(loan, days_left)
            notifier.send(member, subject, body)
            sent += 1
    return sent

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from .errors import StorageCorruptError

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
# A library has no business configuring logging for the program that imports
# it; the null handler keeps "no handlers could be found" off a quiet console.
logger.addHandler(logging.NullHandler())


class JsonStore:
    """Keeps the service's tables as one JSON file per table.

    A table is a list of records; nothing here knows what a record means.
    """

    def __init__(self, root: Path) -> None:
        self.root = Path(root)

    def read(self, table: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Every record in ``table``; one that was never written reads empty."""
        path = self.path_for(table)
        if not path.exists():
            return []
        try:
            records = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise StorageCorruptError(table, str(exc)) from exc
        if not isinstance(records, list):
            raise StorageCorruptError(table, "the stored value is not a list of records")
        return records

    def write(self, table: str, records: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
        """Replace every record in ``table``.

        The new file is written beside the old one and renamed over it, so a
        reader never sees a half-written table.
        """
        # Only the write path needs this, and writing is the rare case.
        import os

        self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path = self.path_for(table)
        scratch = path.with_name(path.name + ".new")
        scratch.write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        os.replace(scratch, path)
        logger.debug("wrote %d records to %s", len(records), path.name)

    def path_for(self, table: str) -> Path:
        """Where ``table`` is kept on disk."""
        return self.root / f"{table}.json"

"""The handlers the counter screen calls."""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date

from bookshelf import BookNotFoundError, api

PRATCHETT = "978-0-00-000001-1"


def test_list_titles_says_how_many_copies_are_free(catalog):
    assert [row["available"] for row in api.list_titles(catalog)] == [1, 2, 0]


def test_borrowing_through_the_handler_returns_the_due_date(catalog, register):
    record = api.borrow_title(register, PRATCHETT, "C-1001", date(2024, 3, 1))
    assert record["due"] == "2024-03-22"


def test_an_expected_failure_is_described_plainly():
    described = api.describe_failure(BookNotFoundError("978-0-00-000999-9"))
    assert described["error"] == "BookNotFoundError"
    assert "978-0-00-000999-9" in described["message"]


def test_an_unexpected_failure_keeps_its_detail_to_itself():
    described = api.describe_failure(ValueError("connection string: hunter2"))
    assert "hunter2" not in described["message"]

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
from bookshelf import Availability, Book, BookNotFoundError, DuplicateBookError

"""Borrowing, renewing and giving books back."""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date

import pytest
from bookshelf import (
    BookUnavailableError,
    LoanNotFoundError,
    RenewalRefusedError,
    overdue_loans,
)

PRATCHETT = "978-0-00-000001-1"
CLARKE = "978-0-00-000002-8"
BORROWED_ON = date(2024, 3, 1)


def test_borrowing_takes_a_copy_off_the_shelf(catalog, register):
    register.borrow(CLARKE, "C-1001", BORROWED_ON)
    assert catalog.copies_available(CLARKE) == 0


def test_the_last_copy_cannot_be_lent_twice(catalog, register):
    register.borrow(CLARKE, "C-1001", BORROWED_ON)
    with pytest.raises(BookUnavailableError):
        register.borrow(CLARKE, "C-1002", BORROWED_ON)


def test_a_loan_can_be_renewed_up_to_the_limit(catalog, register):
    register.borrow(PRATCHETT, "C-1001", BORROWED_ON)
    register.renew(PRATCHETT, "C-1001", BORROWED_ON)
    register.renew(PRATCHETT, "C-1001", BORROWED_ON)
    with pytest.raises(RenewalRefusedError):
        register.renew(PRATCHETT, "C-1001", BORROWED_ON)


def test_giving_back_a_book_nobody_borrowed_is_refused(register):
    with pytest.raises(LoanNotFoundError):
        register.give_back(PRATCHETT, "C-1001")


def test_overdue_loans_are_listed_once_the_due_date_has_passed(catalog, register):
    register.borrow(PRATCHETT, "C-1001", BORROWED_ON)
    assert [loan.isbn for loan in overdue_loans(register, date(2024, 5, 1))] == [PRATCHETT]

"""Reminders sent to members about books that are nearly due."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from datetime import date

from bookshelf import Member, RecordingNotifier
from bookshelf.notifications import remind_member

PRATCHETT = "978-0-00-000001-1"
MEMBER = Member(card_number="C-1001", name="Ada Okonjo", email="ada@example.invalid")


def test_a_reminder_goes_out_when_a_loan_is_nearly_due(catalog, register):
    register.borrow(PRATCHETT, "C-1001", date(2024, 3, 1))
    notifier = RecordingNotifier()
    sent = asyncio.run(remind_member(notifier, MEMBER, register.loans(), date(2024, 3, 20)))
    assert sent == 1
    assert "due back in 2 days" in notifier.sent[0].subject


def test_nothing_goes_out_while_a_loan_still_has_weeks_to_run(catalog, register):
    register.borrow(PRATCHETT, "C-1001", date(2024, 3, 1))
    notifier = RecordingNotifier()
    sent = asyncio.run(remind_member(notifier, MEMBER, register.loans(), date(2024, 3, 2)))
    assert sent == 0
    assert notifier.sent == []
